studies.label: 2 x 2 factorial experiment (GenAI vs no GenAI x individual vs dyad), innovation challenge

arms.name: Individual No AI
arms.description: Worked alone without GenAI on the innovation challenge; the problem-solving phase lasted 90 minutes (PDF p. 5, Procedures). Analyzed count is the Individual No AI N in Table 2 (PDF p. 6).

arms.name: Team No AI
arms.description: Worked in dyads without GenAI during the 90-minute problem-solving phase (PDF p. 5, Procedures). Table 2 prints N = 95, without defining whether it counts people, dyads, or analysis rows; analyzed people and cluster counts remain null (PDF p. 6).

arms.name: Individual AI
arms.description: Worked alone with GPT-4 during the 90-minute problem-solving phase after a 45-minute prompt-engineering and hands-on GPT-4 training module (PDF p. 5, Procedures). Analyzed count is the Individual AI N in Table 2 (PDF p. 6).

arms.name: Team AI
arms.description: Worked in dyads with GPT-4 during the 90-minute problem-solving phase after the same 45-minute AI training module (PDF p. 5, Procedures). Table 2 prints N = 94, without defining whether it counts people, dyads, or analysis rows; analyzed people and cluster counts remain null (PDF p. 6).

studies.task: Produce a solution to an open-ended organizational innovation challenge, such as developing a novel digital product, reimagining customer service, or integrating sustainability into an existing offering (PDF p. 5, Procedures).

ai_tool.name: GPT-4
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Procedures; PDF p. 7, Illustrative cases of assimilation vs. accommodation (participant prompt histories). The paper does not state the model release year or snapshot.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Independent expert raters, blind to condition and participant identity, scored each solution on a 10-point Likert scale adapted from Dell’Acqua et al. (2025). The paper reports ICC2 = 0.51 for these innovation ratings, but does not state the rater count or rating aggregation (PDF p. 5, Measures).

regression.model: OLS, Table 3, with rows for GenAI (vs. no AI), Collaboration (team), and GenAI × Team. The Data analysis strategy says gender, role, and prior AI experience were included where relevant; exact model specifications and analysis N are not printed. Outcome scaling, coefficient standardization, and the SE estimator are not stated. The Results text identifies the quality GenAI coefficient as the individual AI-versus-no-AI comparison; the parallel predictor structure is used for the other outcomes.

estimates.notes: Full randomized individual-cell comparison, without conditioning on observed cognitive strategy or emotion. The person counts come from the individual rows of Table 2, not from an explicitly reported regression N; the combined contrast total is not printed and is left null. Table 3 calls the coefficient β without defining standardization, so outcome_scale is null and no standardized paper effect is assigned. Its regression may include team observations whose aggregation is unspecified; se_basis is therefore unclear. Unit and SD level remain null because the paper does not describe rating aggregation. The coefficient is associated with this cell contrast following the Results interpretation for quality and the parallel predictor structure for the other outcomes; this mapping needs confirmation from the model specification. No arm difference or standardized effect is calculated.

not_extracted.what: Positive emotional change / positive emotional engagement
not_extracted.reason: Pre-task to post-task self-reported affect, rather than a score on the produced solution (PDF p. 6, Measures and Table 2; PDF p. 8, Table 6; PDF p. 10, Appendix A).

not_extracted.what: Negative emotional change / frustration and anxiety
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported affect rather than a score on the produced solution (PDF p. 6, Measures and Table 2; PDF p. 10, Appendix A).

not_extracted.what: Perceived performance: perceived relative solution quality and perceived feasibility
not_extracted.reason: Appendix A lists supplementary participant self-ratings; they are not independent scores on outputs, and numerical arm contrasts are not reported (PDF p. 10, Appendix A).

not_extracted.what: Technology acceptance: intention to reuse GenAI and confidence in GenAI as a collaborator
not_extracted.reason: Attitude and intention measures; no eligible output score or numerical arm contrast is reported (PDF p. 10, Appendix A).

Post-task process measures constructed from self-reports, prompt histories, solutions, and interviews; used as observed mediators rather than randomized assistance configurations or creativity scores (PDF p. 5, Measures; PDF p. 10, Appendix A). The continuous-accommodation robustness analysis is described without numerical results.

not_extracted.what: Open-ended reflections, prompt-history examples, and qualitative interview cases
not_extracted.reason: Qualitative process evidence rather than full-sample quantitative arm contrasts on output creativity (PDF p. 7, Illustrative cases of assimilation vs. accommodation; PDF p. 10, Appendix A).

not_extracted.what: Mediation: direct GenAI effects, indirect effects through accommodation, and mediated proportions for quality, novelty, feasibility, and integration
not_extracted.reason: Mediation analyses are excluded. The direct effects condition on post-treatment accommodation and are not total randomized treatment effects (PDF p. 6, Data analysis strategy; PDF p. 7, Table 4).

not_extracted.what: Moderated mediation: emotional-engagement interaction effects for quality, novelty, feasibility, and integration
not_extracted.reason: Moderation of an observed post-treatment mediator by post-task emotion; excluded moderation/mediation analyses (PDF p. 7, Moderated mediation by emotional engagement; PDF p. 8, Table 5).

not_extracted.what: Accommodation-versus-assimilation performance, integration, and emotion contrasts, including team-versus-individual accommodation
not_extracted.reason: Cognitive strategy is classified after treatment, not randomly assigned. These are strategy-based subgroup/process comparisons, not AI-configuration experiments. The main Results explanation of H2–3 concerns accommodation within teams versus individuals (PDF p. 5, Measures; PDF p. 7, Moderated mediation by emotional engagement; PDF p. 8, Table 6).

not_extracted.what: GenAI × Team coefficients for quality, novelty, feasibility, and integration
not_extracted.reason: Interaction/moderation coefficients, not identified pairwise contrasts between named arms. The paper does not supply reference coding sufficient to reinterpret them as Team AI versus Team No AI or Team AI versus Individual AI. They are not added to the GenAI main effects to manufacture a contrast (PDF p. 6, Table 3 and Effects of GenAI and collaboration structure).

not_extracted.what: Collaboration (team) coefficients for quality, novelty, feasibility, and integration
not_extracted.reason: These do not identify an AI-versus-comparison or AI-configuration contrast. The Results text describes the quality coefficient as teams without GenAI versus individuals without it (PDF p. 6, Table 3 and Effects of GenAI and collaboration structure).

not_extracted.what: Table 6 H1–2 team effect on innovation quality
not_extracted.reason: The summary table labels a team-versus-individual effect without identifying AI-specific arms, the underlying model, its scaling, or its sample. Its coefficient is inconsistent with the team terms in Table 3 and cannot be assigned to a new eligible arm contrast (PDF p. 8, Table 6; PDF p. 6, Table 3 and Results).

open_items: The unit of randomization and the timing and method of dyad formation are not stated. Individual stratification variables do not establish individual allocation; assignment_unit and clusters_per_arm remain null (PDF p. 5, Procedures).

Table 2 prints Team No AI N = 95 and Team AI N = 94, but does not define the counting unit; the odd team count is unexplained for a dyad design. The numbers of analyzed people, dyads, and distinct team outputs need clarification (PDF pp. 5-6, Procedures and Table 2).

The reported 371 is explicitly a recruited count. Assignment counts, exclusions, attrition, the total analyzed headcount, and model-specific N are not supplied. Individual-arm analyzed counts are supported by Table 2, but no contrast total is printed (PDF pp. 5-6; PDF p. 10, Appendix A).

The expert-rater count, aggregation of raters within solutions, handling of shared dyad outputs, and the level over which the Table 2 SDs are computed are not stated. Participant- or team-level SDs and valid independent-unit uncertainty cannot be established for every comparison (PDF pp. 5-6, Measures and Data analysis strategy).

Table 3 labels coefficients β without saying whether coefficients or outcomes are standardized. Exact covariates, predictor coding, model N, SE method, and the relationship to Table 2 means are unspecified. Regression outcome_scale is null; the individual-cell coefficient mapping follows the quality Results text and requires confirmation for the parallel models (PDF p. 6).

The GenAI × Team rows are described as strong team outcomes in the prose, but the reference comparison is not defined. No direct Team AI-versus-Team No AI coefficient or uncertainty is printed, and no unambiguous full-sample Team AI-versus-Individual AI coefficient is identified (PDF p. 6, Table 3; PDF pp. 7-8, H2–3 discussion and Table 6).

The Table 6 H1–2 team coefficient differs from the Table 3 collaboration and interaction coefficients, with no alternative model or contrast explanation. It is not used to replace or supplement the arm contrasts (PDF pp. 6 and 8).
The AI arms received a 45-minute prompt-engineering and GPT-4 training module. The activity or training received by the no-AI arms during that interval is not described (PDF p. 5, Procedures).
GPT-4 is named, but its release year, precise model snapshot, and the dates of the experiment are not stated; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF p. 5, Procedures).
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-11. The complete markdown conversion was read in order, including Appendix A and references. Cited PDF pages 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 were independently text-extracted with pymupdf; all extracted arm statistics and regression cells were checked against PDF p. 6. PDF and printed page numbers agree. Table 2 supplies the two within-factor AI-versus-no-AI comparisons for each eligible output outcome; no strategy-selected subgroup or mediation result is included. No means, differences, totals, SDs, SEs, effect sizes, or intervals were calculated. The design is coded lab_rct because Procedures describe an assigned task in a controlled virtual environment, although the abstract calls it a field experiment (PDF pp. 1 and 5). The paper does not identify a preregistration, a single primary outcome, or participant overlap with another paper. Dell’Acqua et al. is cited as a source of the rating scale, not as a shared sample (PDF p. 5). No across-people diversity or unassisted follow-up outcome is reported. Data are available on request, with no posted dataset URL (PDF p. 9, Data availability). Unknown fields are left null; the uncertainty and model ambiguities from the reconciled screening form remain open.
